chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abdul Kareem, from Sama'ah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'So whoever is forgiven something by his brother, then follow it with good conduct and pay it with kindness.' What is that thing? He said: It is the man who accepts the wergild (blood money). So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, commanded the man who has the right to follow it with good conduct and not make it difficult for him, and commanded the one upon whom the right lies to pay it with kindness when he is financially solvent.

I said, 'What is your view of His Words, Mighty and Majestic: 'So whoever exceeds the limit after this, then for him is a painful punishment'?' He said: 'It is the man who accepts the wergild or reconciles, then comes after that and tortures or kills, so Allah has promised him a painful punishment.'

key_terms.الدِّيَة: Wergild or blood money paid to the victim's heirs
key_terms.فَمَنْ عُفِيَ لَهُ: So whoever is forgiven something (referring to the right of blood money)

ai.seo_question: How does the Imam explain the meaning of 'following with good conduct' and 'exceeding the limit' in the verse of blood money (2:178)?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the practical application of Quran 2:178, defining 'following with good conduct' as the heir's forbearance and 'paying with kindness' as the payer's generous fulfillment of the debt. It further interprets 'exceeding the limit' as post-agreement injustice, such as torture or killing, which triggers divine punishment. This interpretation highlights the Shia emphasis on moral etiquette (adab) in financial settlements and the transition from civil compensation to retribution or punishment upon breach of good faith.
